evidence: The diff hunk shows _copy's missing-source arm raising Reason.SEED_MISSING, and capture of a declared-but-never-up profile reaches it; the agent admits it had only reordered the message, not the slug. A distinct PROFILE_NO_DATA separates a different next move (run crom up), which is what the reason table exists for.
guidance_note: When reusing an error path written for one caller (seed) for a new caller (capture), walk each reason it can raise and ask whether the slug still names the caller's next move.

evidence: The --json prose list was updated to name snapshot while the ## Commands table, which has no test guarding it, was not; the agent's reply confirms the guarded copy moved and the unguarded one did not.
guidance_note: When adding a command, grep the README for every enumeration of commands (tables, exception lists, path listings), not only the ones a test guards.

evidence: cli.main.commands yields the snapshot group, not its nested capture, so the readying sweeps never touched the nested command; the agent added the requested nested-readying test plus an _invocations() walk. single-enforcer is about one runtime enforcer of a rule, and was stretched here to argue test structure.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces a tree-walk because list_commands stops at groups, grep for every other caller of list_commands and route all of them through it in the same commit.

evidence: The hunk's snapshot_dir docstring says 'Capture, `snapshot:` seeding and removal all arrive through it' while only capture exists in the PR; the agent agreed and removed the two nonexistent callers.
guidance_note: Before writing docs for one slice of a multi-ticket feature, grep every new docstring, help text and README row for claims about sibling tickets' unbuilt behavior.

evidence: The agent showed `git ls-tree origin/master -- docs/` listing docs/snapshots.md from #62, and independently crom#64/F2's reviewer quotes 'The repo's own docs/snapshots.md' from master, so the file existed and the reviewer judged from the diff alone.

The hunk's CLI test battery covers SEED_BUSY, SNAPSHOT_EXISTS, INVALID_NAME and PROFILE_UNKNOWN but not PROFILE_UNCLEAN, the only new Reason. The reply-hint says pushback, but the agent wrote 'Plan: valid' and added the test.
guidance_note: When a feature adds new failure reasons, write one end-to-end CLI test per new reason, the same way the existing reasons are covered.

evidence: The hunk shows the destination.exists() check made under seed.profile_lock(profile), which is keyed on the source, so two captures of different profiles to one name both pass it and the loser hits ENOTEMPTY from os.replace instead of SNAPSHOT_EXISTS. The agent admits it had weighed this race and accepted it.
guidance_note: When a check-then-create guards a named resource, take the lock keyed on that resource, not the lock of a neighboring one, the way materialize_under_lock already does.

evidence: Same race as F7: the existence check is not exclusive against captures of other profiles to the same name. It was fixed by the same locking.exclusive(destination) in 3e6b53a.
This duplicates F7's race on the source-keyed lock, and the same destination-lock fix and concurrency test resolve it.
This duplicates F7, and correctly notes that the atomic rename prevents data corruption but breaks the promised SNAPSHOT_EXISTS contract. It was fixed by the same commit.
This duplicates F6 (no CLI-level PROFILE_UNCLEAN test). The reply-hint says pushback, but the reply says 'Plan: valid' and the test was added in 3e6b53a.
This is a third copy of F6. The agent accepted it and pointed to the same added test, despite the pushback reply-hint.

The hunk shows _quiet reading _SINGLETONS once before the copy, while _undisturbed reads before and after and _held treats a dead pid as free. A browser that opens, writes and crashes mid-copy therefore commits a torn snapshot. The agent made the residue read symmetric and handled the still-running case.
guidance_note: When nesting a new check inside an existing before/after guard, give it the same before-and-after shape as the guard it nests in.

evidence: The hunk shows F1's fix placing `if not profile.profile_dir.exists()` 'Before either lock', so a racing crom rm can still land the caller in _copy's SEED_MISSING arm, the outcome F1 was fixed to prevent. F1's own reply cited rm's check as the house pattern, but rm reads the same fact inside seed.profile_lock.
guidance_note: When copying a sibling's check of a fact (rm's profile_dir.exists()), copy where it sits relative to the locks too, not only the predicate.

evidence: The agent confirmed the leak and found it worse than stated (reclaim.deletable returns Refused(STAGING_UNKNOWN) for anything outside doctor.survey). It deferred the fix to ticket crom-seeds-6a5.4 because Staged/Unscanned carry a namespace that snapshots lack, a reasoned design deferral. It declined the docstring note as a second copy of the ticket's fact.
guidance_note: When reusing _staged under a new root, check whether doctor/clean scan that root, and file the gap on the owning ticket before review rather than after.

evidence: The group header 'A seed directory crom will not or cannot copy.' scopes SEED_BUSY to seeding, while test_capturing_a_profile_a_browser_is_writing_is_refused_by_name asserts SEED_BUSY from crom snapshot capture. The drift is from the original PR's reuse of the machinery, not from a review fix.
guidance_note: When generalizing shared machinery to a second caller, grep every comment and header that names the first caller (here 'seed') and generalize all of them in one pass.

evidence: The README's 'Repairs crom makes for you' names down/rm as the only exceptions to auto-declaring, while snapshot capture is a third (session.profile, pinned by test_capture_declares_no_profile_it_was_asked_to_copy). F2's fix diagnosed exactly this class (unguarded README enumerations miss new commands) but added only the Commands-table row.
guidance_note: When a reviewer finds one unguarded README enumeration missing a new command, sweep every README section that lists commands or behaviors for the same omission before pushing.

evidence: paths.snapshots_root() returns state_home()/'snapshots', a new on-disk tree missing from 'Where things live'. The agent called it 'Same class as the exception-list finding', which is the same README sweep F2's fix skipped.
guidance_note: When adding a new paths.* root, add it to the README's on-disk listing in the same change.

evidence: _undisturbed's docstring still said 'the seed's ancestry' after the original PR generalized _refuse and _copy wording for capture. The nesting under _quiet predates review, so this is an original-PR miss, not fix-caused.
guidance_note: When scrubbing caller-specific wording from shared helpers, grep the whole module for the word ('seed') rather than fixing the helpers you happen to touch.

evidence: The two pre-copy refusal tests asserted only that destination is absent, while _staged creates the staging dir before _quiet's checks run. LiveSeedTest already had the empty-parent assertion to copy.
guidance_note: When a test class asserts a cleanup guarantee on some failure paths, apply the same assertion to every failure-path test in the class.

evidence: start_under_lock logs before a comparable copy because 'an unexplained pause looks like a hang', and capture copies hundreds of MB under two locks with no log= seam. one-type-per-behavior concerns types and was pasted onto 'reuse the existing progress convention'.
guidance_note: When adding an operation that does the same heavy work as an existing one, copy that operation's log= seam and pre-work message along with its locking.

evidence: The README row added by F2's fix reads 'copy a stopped profile's data under a name, for other' (profiles to start from), and snapshot_cmd's help claims snapshots seed other profiles, while model.Seed has no snapshot variant. The agent conceded it was 'the same overclaim I already agreed to fix in paths.snapshot_dir's docstring'.
guidance_note: When fixing one overclaim about an unbuilt sibling feature, grep all user-facing copy (help text, README, the row being written in the same fix) for the same claim.

evidence: This repeats F5. The agent showed `git ls-tree 64cb8a7 --name-only docs/` listing docs/snapshots.md, from #62, which the branch descends from, and crom#64/F2 independently quotes that file on master. Re-committing it would create a second copy.
The hunk shows CaptureTest appended after `if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()`. The agent reproduced it: direct invocation ran 32 tests and reported OK, while discover ran 43.
guidance_note: When appending a test class to an existing file, add it above the `__main__` block, and run the file directly once to compare test counts.

evidence: F3's fix introduced _invocations() because list_commands stops at groups, but routed only the readying sweeps through it. _commands_offering_json, _commands_offering_no_probe and the markup sweep kept reading main.list_commands(None) and stayed blind to snapshot capture.
guidance_note: When a finding diagnoses that an enumeration helper misses nested commands, grep every consumer of that enumeration and convert them all in the first fix.

evidence: CromSubGroup extended click.Group, so `crom snapshot captur` got no near-match suggestion. The agent inverted the inheritance (CromGroup derives from CromSubGroup, _sections supplies the no-match value) instead of copying the method, a sound alternative. dataflow-not-control-flow fits, but one-way-deps (module dependency direction) is stretched onto class inheritance.
guidance_note: When writing a sibling of an existing class, list every behavior of the original and justify each one left out in the docstring, rather than only the ones that came to mind.

evidence: _dead_pid() in test_cli.py duplicates test_seed.py's helper. Per F6's reply ('The dead pid is load-bearing in the setup'), it arrived with the PROFILE_UNCLEAN CLI test added in 3e6b53a. The PR closed unmerged with no reply, and the packet does not show why.
guidance_note: When a fix needs a helper that already exists in a sibling test file, move it to shared test support instead of pasting a copy.

evidence: F20's fix added the empty-parent iterdir assertion to the two pre-copy refusal tests and claimed 'all four of capture's failure paths are held'. The still-running post-copy test added for F13 still asserts only destination absence. The PR closed with no reply, for reasons the packet does not show.
guidance_note: When adding an assertion for parity across failure-path tests, enumerate the tests by the raise sites they cover, including ones added in the same review cycle, rather than by the reviewer's list.

evidence: F2's reply itself diagnosed that the Commands table drifted because no test guards it, yet the fix only added the row. Round 3 asks for the guard using the _runnable() walk that now exists. The PR closed with no reply, and the packet does not show why.
guidance_note: When the diagnosis of a drift is 'this copy has no test cross-check', add the cross-check in the same fix, not just the missing entry.

narrative: Round 0 raised real issues (a missing reason slug, a destination race reported four times, a one-sided crash check, doc and test gaps) plus a false 'docs/snapshots.md does not exist' that the agent correctly refuted twice. Most later findings were sweeps the agent's own diagnoses had already named but not applied: one README enumeration fixed and the rest left, one list_commands consumer walked and three left, one overclaim removed and the same one written into the new README row. Round 3 consisted only of fix-caused findings (duplicated _dead_pid, a parity assertion missed by F20's fix, the unguarded Commands table F2 diagnosed). The PR closed unmerged with them unanswered.
guidance_observations: The agent repeatedly diagnosed a class of gap (unguarded README copies, list_commands not descending, overclaims about unbuilt tickets) and then fixed only the instance cited, so each class came back a round later.
The reply-hint read 'pushback' on three threads (F6, F11, F12) where the agent accepted. Reply openings that start with 'Plan: valid' after other text should not be read as pushback.
The reviewer was given a shallow, diff-only view and twice claimed a master file was missing. Repo-wide existence claims from this reviewer need checking against HEAD.

evidence: The agent verified that `ls LICENSE* COPYING*` finds nothing and pyproject declares no license, so `"license": "MIT"` in plugin.json was an unbacked grant. Dropping it, rather than choosing a license for the owner, was the right half of the reviewer's two options.
guidance_note: When filling a manifest from a template, check every metadata field (license, author, homepage) against a fact already in the repo, and omit any that nothing backs.

evidence: The SKILL.md documented `crom snapshot capture`, which existed only on the unmerged #63 branch that the author's installed binary came from. `git grep snapshot -- crom/` on master was empty, and #63 in this batch indeed closed unmerged.
guidance_note: Verify documented commands against the merge target (`git show master:crom/`), never against the binary on PATH, which may be built from an unmerged branch.

narrative: Two correct round-0 findings: an unbacked MIT license field and a skill section documenting a command that existed only on the unmerged #63 branch. The agent removed both, then re-verified every command, flag and value in the skill against master rather than the installed binary. Round 1 approved with no findings.
guidance_observations: The S5 finding came from verifying behavior against a locally installed binary built from another PR's branch. The agent's own follow-up check against master is the move that should precede shipping docs.
